title: Ulyana and the Visitor
premise: Dominic Brightwater, a hospice nurse who documents the strange habit of the dying counting backwards, takes a live-in post at Marrow House, where every mirror lags one second behind reality. The lag is not a haunting but a debt: in 1974, the house's founder stole a dying woman's final breath to extend her own life, and the mirrors have been holding that stolen second ever since. As the last resident, elderly Edith Vane, prepares to sign papers transferring the house, Dominic discovers their own name written in the 1974 ledger — they were the child who was taken. In the climax, Dominic returns the stolen breath through the lagging mirror during Edith's final hours, unmaking the founder's immortality and freeing the house; they end no longer invisible, but bound to Marrow House as its keeper of records.
about_author: Ines Ashgrove is the pen name of a former night-shift archivist who spent years cataloguing the belongings of the deceased and swears some boxes were heavier than they should have been. They write horror about paperwork, inheritance, and the terrible intimacy of strangers' last days.

chapters.title: The Second That Isn't Ours
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Arriving at Marrow House for a live-in hospice posting, Dominic notices the dying residents counting backwards from numbers that don't match their ages, and records it faithfully in their journal. The emotional beat is wary belonging: Dominic, habitually invisible, begins to feel watched by the house itself when a hallway mirror reflects them a beat too late.

chapters.title: Ledger of 1974
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with interludes from Edith's failing memory. Investigating the basement archive, Dominic finds a ledger from 1974 recording a 'transfer' signed by the house's founder, Marguerite Vane, alongside a child's name: Brightwater. The emotional beat is dread curdling into recognition as Dominic realizes the debt involves them personally, while Edith grows terrified of signing anything.

chapters.title: What the Mirrors Hold
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The lag worsens — reflections act independently, showing 1974 scenes and a woman breathing out instead of in. Marguerite's preserved presence, sustained by the stolen breath, tries to bargain: let Edith sign, stay invisible forever, be safe. The emotional beat is loyalty versus truth, as Dominic must choose between the comfort of anonymity and exposing what they are.

chapters.title: Counting Forwards
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV at Edith's deathbed. Refusing the bargain, Dominic enters the mirror's held second and returns the stolen breath to the dying woman of 1974, collapsing Marguerite's borrowed life as Edith signs nothing and dies free. The emotional beat is release: the mirrors catch up, the counting stops, and Dominic stays on — visible, named, keeper of the record.
